claims.statement: Sangam Pitch is a third deep agent exposed at /proposal as sangam_proposal. It is built by build_proposal_agent in lifespan._build_agents, its access dependency is proposal_chat_access in AGENT_ACCESS (a path missing from that table fails at boot), and it runs with emit_raw_events=False.

proposal_chat_access derives everything from a per-person thread id proposal-<proposal id>-<user id>: another person's thread or an org the caller cannot read is 404, a member who cannot edit gets 403, and it sets chat_user_id, chat_scope and chat_proposal. The model never names the proposal: context.current() reads the chat_proposal ContextVar and re-reads that proposal row on every call, and no tool takes a proposal id.

The caller-scope edit rule is that staff, an org's admins and its stewards edit a proposal while members only read. It is enforced three ways: 0048's RLS write policies (my_match_org_ids or is_staff), CallerScope.can_edit_proposal, and the can_edit column in repository queries. Agent tools run on the owner pool past RLS, so every write tool calls require_edit first and returns a REFUSED string for a reader; REST writes return 403.

Proposals are stored server-side: migration 0048 adds work and summary jsonb columns to proposals. New proposals are created from a saved Funder Match run (409 without one, 403 unless admin, steward or staff), with work seeded at stage 1 from the match, the funder's proposal_template document, and the default style; the list endpoint reads only summary, never work.

work.apply is the single write path to proposals.work: repo.save locks the row FOR UPDATE and calls apply, which validates every change against allowed path patterns before applying any (so nothing is half-applied), requires a section change to carry its rev (stale rev raises StaleSection, a 409 naming who changed it), bumps rev, logs each change with who, via, from and to, and recomputes the part's untraced list and the summary.

apply restricts who may set certain paths by via: stage moves forward only through advance (PATCH only goes back); score, needs_rewrite, used_in, new facts, questions and readers are agent-only; missing and untraced are code-derived; polished and versions are set only by the polish and version routes (a version list must grow by exactly one numbered entry); a person may set a fact status only to proposed, confirmed or rejected, and a correction is expanded into a new you_said fact with supersedes plus the old fact marked corrected.

Code owns the steps. work.stage has four stages, and steps.exit_check(stage, work) returns what is missing: step 1 needs every requirement answered with no hard No, step 2 needs a form chosen or skipped, a style, readers started and none still running (a running reader older than 30 minutes counts as dead), step 3 is always leavable, step 4 is last. REST POST /advance (409 with the missing list) and the agent's advance_step (NOT YET) both call it inside the row lock.

Writing tools refuse themselves in code, not the prompt: steps.too_early blocks add_facts and read_files before step 2 and ask_user, write_section and suggest_edit before step 3; steps.may_write enforces section dependency order from rubric.DEPENDS_ON (A2 and A3 before A4, A4 before A5 and A6, A5 before A15, every other section before the Summary A1), waived for the part the person has open on screen.

Step 1's requirements are built by gates.build from the saved Funder Match detail: 12A, 80G, audited accounts, CSR Form 1 for Section 135 funders (the only hard requirement), plus one soft requirement per not_judged line beginning with the funder's own bar. earlier_phase comes from the match's relationship points and adds section F4.

Facts live in work.facts (ids kN, cited as ⟦kN⟧) with no separate table. reliability.tier colours a fact by origin alone (registry and vault green, web and derived amber, you_said its own). add_facts is the agent's only way to add facts and code checks each source: registry markers are re-read from the record and the value must appear, vault facts must cite a ticked file with valid quoted evidence (and a reader may cite only the file it was given), web facts need an http link and at least 20 quoted characters, derived facts name their source facts, and you_said facts are never added there. Identical facts return the existing id, and new facts arrive proposed.

ask_user pauses the graph with a LangGraph interrupt of type proposal_question, and questions.may_ask is the code gate: not before step 3, on step 3 only about the part open on screen, one open question per person, a gap open with a teammate is refused, and the reason (missing, disagree, org_call) must be warranted by the fact list. Questions live in work.questions with who they were asked of. Typed replies are sorted as answer, question back or skip by a utility-model call (a failure counts as a question back); an answer is stored as a confirmed you_said fact and a skip parks the question for whoever opens that part next.

Readers are launched by code, not by the model: readers.read claims pending readers (every ticked file, the funder side, and public research when built) under the row lock, marking them running in work.readers (a second press while a non-stale reader runs is refused as Busy), then runs one reader per key with asyncio.gather bounded by max_parallel_research. Each reader is a separate checkpointer-less deep agent on research_model with tool_errors and RunSources middleware; file and funder readers have no web tool, a file reader's RunSources limits it to its one file and the funder reader opens none of the org's files. Each clears the inherited run config so its steps do not stream into the chat. Outcomes are recorded per reader, one failure never stops the others, a saved link with no stored file is marked failed without running a reader, and Try again re-reads only what failed.

write_section runs code checks before saving: edit rights, step, section existence, text length, dependency order, then trace.check per paragraph, where every number, rupee amount (lakh and crore compared as rupees), place and partner name must appear in a live fact that the same paragraph cites as ⟦kN⟧ (years, FY ranges and Schedule VII clauses and [Add: ...] gaps are exempt; citing a missing, corrected or rejected fact is refused). A refusal names each untraced claim.

After tracing, write_section grades the text with one utility-model call that lists missing strong elements (none missing scores 2, one scores 1, more scores 0). A grader failure never blocks the save. The save goes through work.apply at the rev the model read, updating each cited fact's used_in, and a teammate's intervening change is refused by name. A6, A15 and F1 below 2 get a rewrite nudge in the tool reply.

suggest_edit proposes better wording for one passage on a proposal_suggestion interrupt card: the passage must appear exactly once, the new wording is trace-checked before the person sees it (only newly untraced claims block it), and only 'Use this' saves it, through the same _store path at the part's current rev; keeping their wording returns KEPT and typed feedback returns FEEDBACK.

A person's own REST edit to a part's text is not refused by the trace check: apply stores untraced claims in the part's untraced list (shown under Fix first), recomputes which facts the part uses, clears done, and clears needs_rewrite, score and missing when the text changed. Marking a part Done makes the save route grade its text once.

Corrections propagate in code: review.follow, called inside work.apply, replaces a corrected value word for word in sentences citing the old fact if the fix adds no untraced claim, otherwise marks the section needs_rewrite (cleared only by a later fully traced save), and sends derived facts worked out from the changed fact back to proposed.

readiness.summary is recomputed on every save and splits what remains into Fix first (blocks ready: unanswered or hard-No requirements, unwritten parts, needs-rewrite or untraced parts, A6/A15/F1 below 2, core parts at 0, used facts still proposed, unsettled disagreements) and Worth checking (never blocks: score 1, will-have-it promises, gaps, parked questions). work.conflicts is initialised and counted but nothing in backend/app writes to it.

POST /polish makes one settings.model call to smooth all written parts, then polish.differences compares trace.extract (figures in rupees, places, names, gaps) before and after: any lost, added or changed claim returns 409 with the differences and stores nothing. The smoothed text is saved only by that route (via=polish) with each part's rev, and assemble.final uses it only for parts unchanged since smoothing.

POST /versions builds a .docx (Summary first, ⟦k⟧ marks removed, [Add: ...] gaps highlighted), uploads it to the org vault at <org>/proposals/<id>/v<N>.docx, inserts a private proposal_draft document marked AI-generated, and appends a version entry with a snapshot of the facts the text cites to work.versions. It needs storage enabled (503 otherwise) and a clash on the version number is refused.

The proposal agent uses the strong model with nine tools (read_proposal, advance_step, read_match, read_org_record, add_facts, ask_user, read_files, write_section, suggest_edit) plus the harness read_file, and middleware, in order: filesystem, tool_errors, nothing_to_answer, clear_old_tool_results, fallback, cheap_summarizer and ProposalContext. There is no deepagents subagent: the readers are separate graphs built in readers.build (with EVIDENCE_TOOLS, FUNDER_TOOLS and PUBLIC_TOOLS) and launched by code.

ProposalContext re-reads the proposal on every model call and adds a stable block (names, step, requirement answers, form, section states; cache breakpoint only for Anthropic models) and a live block (what blocks the step, edit rights, on-screen part, rewrite flags, changes outside this chat from work.log including the person's own clicks, file readings, waiting questions), never saved. The screen state is client input that only sets focus: unknown part codes are dropped, and the screen line is also appended to the latest human message.

Agent tools never raise: each catches failures and returns a string (REFUSED, NOT YET, or tool failed with the exception name) so the model reads the refusal. The only exception re-raised is LangGraph's GraphBubbleUp in ask_user and suggest_edit, which is the interrupt pause itself.

The copilot's shipped milestones (M2 to M8, including suggest_edit and write in place) are recorded in the changelog's Proposals section, and the public research reader is recorded there as unmerged although its code exists. The Not finished table has no copilot or public-research row, and its row for 2026-10-10-list-pages-proposals-media.md still says 'No proposals backend', which no longer matches the code. The plan's own Later list (freshness colours, flag_conflict, form limits and others) is not built, while its landscape reader was replaced by public research; the plan's StageGate, AskGate and ProposalSources middleware do not exist because those checks live inside the tools, and the only proposal-specific agent middleware are ProposalContext and the small nothing_to_answer hook (PublicGuard belongs to the public reader).

Proposals are no longer kept in browser localStorage: the frontend retains only hadBrowserProposals(), which checks the legacy sangam.proposals.v1 key for drafts left in one browser, while the proposals table (created in 0009) is extended by migration 0048 with work and summary and is read and written by the backend.

The tool_errors middleware is a backstop on the proposal agent and on every reader: a tool that raises past its own try/except answers the model with '<tool> failed: <ExceptionName>' (type only, so no SQL, paths or keys leak) instead of ending the run.

Public research is a third reader (work.readers key public) built only when settings.tavily_api_key is set; without a key pending never lists it and nothing fails. Its task is built from the registry's public rows (places, themes, programmes, SDGs) and the sections public facts can serve, never from files or the fact list, and it names the org only as someone never to search for. It is the only reader with web access (Sources(web=True), tools search_public_sources, read_page, fetch_document, read_document_pages and add_facts).

Public research is guarded in code: PublicGuard refuses a search_public_sources query that names the org on a word boundary and keeps the text of every page it reads (read_page, and fetched PDFs via read_document_pages, keyed by a normalised page_key); while the run's PUBLIC_RUN is set, add_facts also applies facts.off_page, which accepts only web facts for A2, A3, A4, A14 and F1 with an as_of year, a link read in this run, a quote found on that page, and every value number present in the quote. Accepted facts are stamped found_by public, which the frontend uses to label them 'From public research' and to tell them from funder-reader web facts.

The nothing_to_answer before_model hook on the proposal agent ends a run without a model call when there are no messages or the last message is an AI reply with no tool calls, because asking Claude to continue its own reply fails with a 400.
